enunciado: O principal objetivo do texto é
texto_apoio:
DIGITAL BANKS AND THE UNBANKED

Over the past decade, digital banks have transformed the way millions of people in emerging markets manage their money. Unlike traditional institutions, which rely on extensive branch networks, these companies operate almost entirely through smartphone apps. This model allows them to cut costs dramatically and, in many cases, offer accounts with no monthly fees.

The impact has been particularly strong among people who were previously excluded from the formal financial system. For them, opening an account no longer requires a trip to a branch, a proof of income or a minimum deposit. As a result, the number of adults with access to a bank account has grown significantly in several countries.

However, rapid growth brings its own challenges. Profitability remains elusive for many digital banks, since low fees also mean low revenue per customer. Some have responded by expanding into lending, a move that increases income but also exposes them to credit risk. Regulators, meanwhile, are paying closer attention to how these firms protect customer data and manage defaults.

Whether digital banks will eventually replace traditional ones is still an open question. What seems certain is that they have forced the entire industry to rethink how it serves its clients.

(Original text written for study purposes.)
alternativas: defender a substituição imediata dos bancos tradicionais pelos bancos digitais.

comentario: O texto apresenta o modelo dos bancos digitais, seu impacto sobre pessoas antes excluídas do sistema financeiro (parágrafo 2) e os desafios de lucratividade, risco de crédito e regulação (parágrafo 3). A substituição dos bancos tradicionais é tratada como “an open question”, não como algo defendido. Os reguladores são apenas mencionados como mais atentos, sem crítica. O texto também não é um tutorial e afirma que a lucratividade “remains elusive”.

texto_apoio:
THE INTEREST RATE DILEMMA

When prices rise across the economy, central banks usually respond by raising interest rates. The logic is straightforward: higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which discourages consumers from buying on credit and companies from taking out loans to expand. With less money chasing the same amount of goods, the pressure on prices tends to ease.

This tool, however, is far from painless. Higher borrowing costs can slow down economic activity, and if rates stay high for too long, unemployment may rise. Central bankers therefore face a delicate balancing act: tighten too little, and inflation persists; tighten too much, and the economy may fall into recession.

Timing adds another layer of difficulty. Changes in interest rates take months, sometimes more than a year, to be fully felt in the economy. This means that decisions must be based on forecasts rather than on current data alone. If the forecasts turn out to be wrong, the central bank may find itself fighting yesterday's problem.

Communication has thus become as important as the decisions themselves. By clearly explaining its intentions, a central bank can influence expectations, and expectations, in turn, shape how businesses set prices and how workers negotiate wages.

(Original text written for study purposes.)

comentario: O parágrafo 1 explica que juros mais altos desestimulam o crédito e aliviam os preços; o parágrafo 2 diz que a medida “is far from painless”, podendo desacelerar a economia e aumentar o desemprego. O crédito é desestimulado, não estimulado. O parágrafo 3 afirma que os efeitos levam meses, às vezes mais de um ano, e que as decisões dependem de previsões, “rather than on current data alone”.

enunciado: A ideia central do texto é que
texto_apoio:
THE WEAKEST LINK

Banks spend billions every year on cybersecurity, yet the most common attacks do not target their systems directly. Instead, criminals target customers. Phishing messages, which imitate official communications, try to persuade people to click on fraudulent links or share their passwords. Because these messages are increasingly well written, even careful users can be fooled.

In response, many banks have adopted multi-factor authentication, which requires customers to confirm their identity in more than one way, such as a password combined with a code sent to their phone. Some institutions also use behavioral analysis: if a customer who usually makes small transfers suddenly tries to send a large sum at midnight, the system may block the transaction until it is confirmed.

Such measures are effective, but they can also frustrate legitimate customers, who may see their payments delayed. Striking the right balance between security and convenience is one of the industry's greatest challenges.

Experts agree on one point: technology alone cannot solve the problem. Unless customers learn to recognize suspicious messages, criminals will keep finding new ways to exploit human trust.

(Original text written for study purposes.)

apesar dos investimentos em segurança, os clientes continuam sendo o principal alvo dos criminosos.

comentario: O texto afirma que os ataques mais comuns “do not target their systems directly” e que os criminosos miram os clientes; conclui que, sem a conscientização do cliente, os golpes continuarão. Por isso, a invasão frequente de sistemas contraria o texto. As medidas são “effective”, mas nada indica que eliminaram fraudes. O texto diz que “even careful users can be fooled” e que “technology alone cannot solve the problem”.

texto_apoio:
GREEN BONDS

Green bonds are debt securities issued to finance projects with environmental benefits, such as renewable energy plants, clean transportation or energy-efficient buildings. Like conventional bonds, they pay investors a fixed income over a set period. The difference lies in how the money raised is used.

The market for these instruments has expanded rapidly since the first issues in the late 2000s. Governments, banks and corporations have all joined in, attracted by growing demand from investors who want their portfolios to reflect environmental concerns. In some cases, issuers have even obtained slightly lower borrowing costs, a benefit sometimes called the “greenium”.

Critics, nevertheless, warn about “greenwashing” — the practice of presenting an investment as more environmentally friendly than it really is. Without clear standards and independent verification, a bond may carry a green label while financing projects of doubtful value. To address this concern, several countries have developed official taxonomies that define which activities qualify as sustainable.

For banks, green finance represents both an opportunity and a responsibility. It opens new lines of business, but it also requires careful analysis to ensure that promises made to investors are actually kept.

(Original text written for study purposes.)

comentario: O texto é explícito: “The difference lies in how the money raised is used”, isto é, no uso do dinheiro captado, destinado a projetos ambientais. A renda fixa e o prazo definido são justamente pontos em comum (“Like conventional bonds, they pay investors a fixed income over a set period”). Governos, bancos e empresas emitem ambos, e o texto não afirma que títulos verdes são livres de risco.

Green bonds are debt securities issued to finance projects with environmental benefits, such as renewable energy plants, clean transportation or energy-efficient buildings. Like conventional bonds, they pay investors a fixed income over a set period. The difference lies in how the money raised is used.

The market for these instruments has expanded rapidly since the first issues in the late 2000s. Governments, banks and corporations have all joined in, attracted by growing demand from investors who want their portfolios to reflect environmental concerns. In some cases, issuers have even obtained slightly lower borrowing costs, a benefit sometimes called the “greenium”.

Critics, nevertheless, warn about “greenwashing” — the practice of presenting an investment as more environmentally friendly than it really is. Without clear standards and independent verification, a bond may carry a green label while financing projects of doubtful value. To address this concern, several countries have developed official taxonomies that define which activities qualify as sustainable.

For banks, green finance represents both an opportunity and a responsibility. It opens new lines of business, but it also requires careful analysis to ensure that promises made to investors are actually kept.

(Original text written for study purposes.)

a apresentação de um investimento como mais sustentável do que ele realmente é.
a classificação oficial das atividades consideradas sustentáveis.
o custo de captação mais baixo obtido por alguns emissores.
a exigência de que os bancos financiem apenas projetos ambientais.
comentario: O texto define “greenwashing” como “the practice of presenting an investment as more environmentally friendly than it really is”. A verificação independente e as taxonomias oficiais são remédios contra o problema, não o próprio problema. O custo de captação menor é o “greenium”, e não há menção a exigência de que bancos financiem só projetos ambientais.

comentario: “They” retoma “green bonds”, sujeito do parágrafo: os títulos verdes pagam renda fixa, assim como os convencionais. “Conventional bonds” aparece dentro da comparação introduzida por “Like” e não é o sujeito de “pay”. Projetos e usinas não pagam renda aos investidores, e “investors” é o objeto que recebe o pagamento.

Para justificar essa preocupação.

comentario: O verbo “address”, aplicado a um problema ou preocupação, significa lidar com ele ou enfrentá-lo. As taxonomias oficiais são criadas para combater o greenwashing, definindo o que é realmente sustentável. O falso cognato com “endereçar” pode levar a “transferir” ou “registrar”, mas nenhuma dessas leituras faz sentido. Divulgar ou justificar a preocupação também não corresponde à função das taxonomias.

alternativas: a um rendimento mais alto garantido aos investidores de títulos verdes.
ao custo de captação ligeiramente menor obtido por alguns emissores de títulos verdes.
a uma taxa extra cobrada dos investidores que compram títulos verdes.
ao selo oficial que certifica um título como sustentável.
ao prêmio pago por governos às empresas que emitem títulos verdes.
comentario: O texto diz que alguns emissores obtiveram “slightly lower borrowing costs, a benefit sometimes called the greenium”. O benefício é de quem emite, não de quem investe; por isso a ideia de rendimento mais alto para o investidor é o contrário. A palavra lembra “premium” (prêmio), o que torna plausíveis as opções de taxa extra ou prêmio governamental, mas nenhuma delas aparece no texto. O selo verde é mencionado em outro contexto, no do greenwashing.
